<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="443.0mm" height="355.6mm" viewBox="0 0 443.0 355.6" data-device="mx480" data-view="front" data-weight-base-kg="29.7" data-weight-max-kg="100.26" data-weight-note="Table 88 (physical specifications) gives 65.5 lb (29.7 kg) for the chassis with midplane, fan tray, air filter and cable management brackets, and 221.03 lb (100.26 kg) for the maximum configuration. The guide's own prose disagrees with the table and is not carried - the rack-requirements and lift text give "up to 163.5 lb (74.2 kg) depending on the configuration" (the source of the 163.5 this file used to carry, where it was misread as kilograms), and the mounting-shelf note gives 128 lb (58.1 kg), which is the MX240's Table 88 maximum." data-throughput="7.5 Tbps-class (datasheet family table)" data-power-typical-w="3470" data-power-envelope="unstated" data-power-typical-scope="AC typical power draw from the MX Series family datasheet, which names no configuration, ambient or side; DC 3150 W" data-base-system-w="40" data-cooling-system-w="160 W high-capacity (110 W normal); dedicated PSU tap" data-max-thermal-output="AC 11,322 BTU/h (3318 W); DC 9,632 BTU/h (2823 W) (Table 89, which calls them estimates; provisioning ceiling)" data-operating-temp="0 C to 40 C" data-storage-temp="-40 C to 70 C" data-humidity="5-90 percent noncondensing" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://support.juniper.net/support/eol/product/m_series/" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='juniper/mx480-craft@'] .state-blinking { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='juniper/mx480-craft@'] .state-blinking { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='juniper/mx480-craft@'] .state-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='juniper/mx480-craft@'] .state-red { --led-color: #d0021b; }
    g[data-ref^='juniper/mx480-craft@'] .state-yellow { --led-color: #f5a623; }
</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="443.0mm" height="622.0mm" viewBox="0 0 443.0 622.0" data-device="mx480" data-view="bottom" data-weight-base-kg="29.7" data-weight-max-kg="100.26" data-weight-note="Table 88 (physical specifications) gives 65.5 lb (29.7 kg) for the chassis with midplane, fan tray, air filter and cable management brackets, and 221.03 lb (100.26 kg) for the maximum configuration. The guide's own prose disagrees with the table and is not carried - the rack-requirements and lift text give "up to 163.5 lb (74.2 kg) depending on the configuration" (the source of the 163.5 this file used to carry, where it was misread as kilograms), and the mounting-shelf note gives 128 lb (58.1 kg), which is the MX240's Table 88 maximum." data-throughput="7.5 Tbps-class (datasheet family table)" data-power-typical-w="3470" data-power-envelope="unstated" data-power-typical-scope="AC typical power draw from the MX Series family datasheet, which names no configuration, ambient or side; DC 3150 W" data-base-system-w="40" data-cooling-system-w="160 W high-capacity (110 W normal); dedicated PSU tap" data-max-thermal-output="AC 11,322 BTU/h (3318 W); DC 9,632 BTU/h (2823 W) (Table 89, which calls them estimates; provisioning ceiling)" data-operating-temp="0 C to 40 C" data-storage-temp="-40 C to 70 C" data-humidity="5-90 percent noncondensing" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://support.juniper.net/support/eol/product/m_series/" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="622.0mm" height="355.6mm" viewBox="0 0 622.0 355.6" data-device="mx480" data-view="left" data-weight-base-kg="29.7" data-weight-max-kg="100.26" data-weight-note="Table 88 (physical specifications) gives 65.5 lb (29.7 kg) for the chassis with midplane, fan tray, air filter and cable management brackets, and 221.03 lb (100.26 kg) for the maximum configuration. The guide's own prose disagrees with the table and is not carried - the rack-requirements and lift text give "up to 163.5 lb (74.2 kg) depending on the configuration" (the source of the 163.5 this file used to carry, where it was misread as kilograms), and the mounting-shelf note gives 128 lb (58.1 kg), which is the MX240's Table 88 maximum." data-throughput="7.5 Tbps-class (datasheet family table)" data-power-typical-w="3470" data-power-envelope="unstated" data-power-typical-scope="AC typical power draw from the MX Series family datasheet, which names no configuration, ambient or side; DC 3150 W" data-base-system-w="40" data-cooling-system-w="160 W high-capacity (110 W normal); dedicated PSU tap" data-max-thermal-output="AC 11,322 BTU/h (3318 W); DC 9,632 BTU/h (2823 W) (Table 89, which calls them estimates; provisioning ceiling)" data-operating-temp="0 C to 40 C" data-storage-temp="-40 C to 70 C" data-humidity="5-90 percent noncondensing" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://support.juniper.net/support/eol/product/m_series/" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="622.0mm" height="355.6mm" viewBox="0 0 622.0 355.6" data-device="mx480" data-view="right" data-weight-base-kg="29.7" data-weight-max-kg="100.26" data-weight-note="Table 88 (physical specifications) gives 65.5 lb (29.7 kg) for the chassis with midplane, fan tray, air filter and cable management brackets, and 221.03 lb (100.26 kg) for the maximum configuration. The guide's own prose disagrees with the table and is not carried - the rack-requirements and lift text give "up to 163.5 lb (74.2 kg) depending on the configuration" (the source of the 163.5 this file used to carry, where it was misread as kilograms), and the mounting-shelf note gives 128 lb (58.1 kg), which is the MX240's Table 88 maximum." data-throughput="7.5 Tbps-class (datasheet family table)" data-power-typical-w="3470" data-power-envelope="unstated" data-power-typical-scope="AC typical power draw from the MX Series family datasheet, which names no configuration, ambient or side; DC 3150 W" data-base-system-w="40" data-cooling-system-w="160 W high-capacity (110 W normal); dedicated PSU tap" data-max-thermal-output="AC 11,322 BTU/h (3318 W); DC 9,632 BTU/h (2823 W) (Table 89, which calls them estimates; provisioning ceiling)" data-operating-temp="0 C to 40 C" data-storage-temp="-40 C to 70 C" data-humidity="5-90 percent noncondensing" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://support.juniper.net/support/eol/product/m_series/" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }

       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */

    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */

      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }

    }
